assembly_rules: every control works or it does not ship

machine.generated_from: contract data + builder-index-v1 (478 pieces, real HTML+CSS)
machine.law: Builders compose from these pieces; they never recreate them.
machine.ship_law: scorecard 9+ -> show Shawn the HTML -> his yeah -> live on its own

promise.big: A fully functioning app that works right away.
promise.sub: Nobody waits through setup to feel the value. You get the finished, working thing on day one — and subtract what you don't want.
promise.rule: The assembler cannot publish anything with an unverified feature, period. Default-on raises the stakes: every standard feature must be proven, or day-one value becomes day-one betrayal.

title: The Smart Builder

gallery.title: Search everything. Swap anything.
gallery.lede: The whole library is searchable and every piece is swappable. Nothing is recreated — the most beautiful thing the builder can do is take our own parts and compose them.
points: Search by name, style, or color.
Type “buttons” — all buttons. “Boards” — all boards. The search engine reads human labels and model numbers alike.
Browse every category laid out — buttons, boards, banners, jewels, lists, forms, navigation — each piece rendered in its real code.
Love the template but want different buttons? Tap + Add on any piece and it swaps in. The tray holds your picks until you say build.
On any template, any piece: “I want button XYZ here” or “make this one coral.” Simple words, applied at build.

customize.title: Your words are the editor.
customize.lede: Change anything — or change nothing and just say what you want. The builder handles the rest.
points: “Swap this button for NAYA-BTN-009.” “Make the banner coral.” Notes land in the contract; the build applies them.
Any piece, any color of the spectrum — or let Naya pick what fits the page.
Move things where you want them. The layout follows your words.
“I want this page but personal to me.” “I want this functionality.” That is a complete instruction.
Love it the way it is? Say so. Done is done.

design.law: spectrum in law order, strict by section position. Hero takes purple (0).

template_ranking.basis: general population daily-use, per Shawn's relayed ranking; usage will re-rank over time — ship it, watch, learn
template_ranking.note: Smart list is NOT a template — it is a standard feature (see standard_features). Twelve stays twelve.

standard_features.law: Every template ships as a complete working app. Standard features are ON by default; the intake is checkmarks, all checked — uncheck what you don't want.

features.label: Smart Lists
features.note: Not a template — the cross-cutting way to organize anything: notes, contacts, topics, posts. Layers into every template.

composition.law: Nobody picks just one. A customer picks multiple templates — or all — and they sync together, hub plus rooms.
composition.model: hub plus rooms, all in sync

activation.law: Enabled by default must not mean connected or publicly shared without consent. (Naya 3's refinement, 2026-10-17)
activation.rule: Features arrive ready-to-use with what is available. External integrations — accounts, credentials, authorization — activate only when the customer explicitly grants permission.
activation.flow: resolver checks implementation + dependencies + permissions -> ready: activates -> missing: the Builder explains precisely what is needed and never pretends the feature works
activation.priority: next implementation: default-feature selection + capability-activation flow. Template ranking stays provisional until usage gives evidence.

architecture.rule: One person, one connected Smart World, many pages and rooms. (Naya 3, 2026-10-17)
architecture.smart_lists: organize any permitted object — notes, posts, contacts, projects, topics
architecture.shared: the underlying identity, relationships, and authorized intelligence remain shared

factory.law: The Smart Builder is a Smart App factory, not a webpage generator. (Naya 3, 2026-10-17)
factory.principle: Don't give people an empty builder and ask them to construct an app. Give them a working Smart App they immediately personalize, simplify, expand, and connect.

privacy_law.law: Privacy is a dial, not a doctrine. Private where it starts, public wherever they take it.
privacy_law.note: Machine key contract['privacy'] carries the enum; this block is the law behind it. Each connection its own switch, each their call.
